options.what: The BoneMap resource that maps source skeleton bone names to SkeletonProfileHumanoid profile bone names. Gateway option: all other retarget/ options are hidden when this is null.

Bakes the scene node's global Transform3D (position, rotation, scale from Node3D ancestors) into the skeleton's bone rests and adjusts animation tracks to compensate. Clears the translation component so the retargeted model sits at the origin.

Sets the skeleton's motion_scale to the absolute Y height of the scale-base bone (typically Hips) in the global rest, then divides all position track values by that motion_scale. Normalises movement magnitude across differently-sized rigs.

When true, resets every bone's pose to the new rest after the rest has been overwritten, so the skeleton starts at the corrected rest. When false, adjusts the existing pose to account for the rest change.

options.type: int (enum: None=0, Overwrite Axis=1, Use Retarget Modifier=2)
options.what: Selects the retargeting strategy. None: no rest adjustment. Overwrite Axis: overwrites each mapped bone's rest to match the profile's reference pose, adjusting animation tracks in-place. Use Retarget Modifier: creates a second profile-shaped skeleton with a RetargetModifier3D that retargets at runtime from the original skeleton.

When retarget_method is Overwrite Axis, unmapped bones that have no mapped descendants keep their original global rest instead of being orphaned by the rest overwrite. Only visible when retarget_method == 1.

When retarget_method is Use Retarget Modifier, selects between global-pose retargeting (the modifier copies source global bone poses directly to the target skeleton) and local-pose retargeting (the modifier decomposes through parent chains). Only visible when retarget_method == 2.

Name given to the original (unmapped) skeleton when retarget_method is Use Retarget Modifier. The profile-shaped skeleton takes the original name; the source skeleton is renamed to this. Only visible when retarget_method == 2.

Enables silhouette fixing: compares each bone's direction (head-to-tail) in the source skeleton against the profile's expected direction, and rotates the source bone's rest to align when the angular difference exceeds the threshold. Compensates for proportion and axis-convention differences between rigs.

Bone names to exclude from silhouette fixing. Filtered bones keep their original rest direction. Useful for bones whose direction is intentionally different from the profile (e.g. tail bones, prop attachments).
Minimum angle in degrees between the source bone direction and the profile direction before silhouette fixing rotates the rest. Bones below the threshold are left alone.
Vertical offset applied to the scale-base bone's rest origin and its position track keys. Adjusts the overall height of the retargeted skeleton relative to the ground.
When true, removes all animation tracks that are not bone TRS (position, rotation, scale on a Skeleton3D bone). Strips non-skeletal tracks like mesh visibility, blend shapes, etc.
When true, removes position tracks on mapped bones except the root bone and the scale-base bone. The engine considers most bone positions to be determined by the rest hierarchy, not animated.
What to do with animation tracks on bones not mapped in the BoneMap. None: keep them. Remove: delete them. Separate Library: move them to a separate AnimationLibrary under the 'unmapped_bones' key.

Renames every source skeleton bone to its SkeletonProfileHumanoid name via the BoneMap. Makes the skeleton's bone names match the profile, which is required for the Use Retarget Modifier method and for cross-rig consistency.
Makes the renamed skeleton a unique node (accessible via %Name in AnimationPlayer paths) and rewrites all animation track paths to use the unique-node prefix.
The name given to the skeleton when make_unique is true. Animation track paths become %GeneralSkeleton:BoneName.

ours.label: SOURCED
ours.note: Both map source bone names to profile/target names. Ours is a hardcoded 22-entry const Dictionary (line 54: const UE4_TO_OURS := {). The engine uses a BoneMap resource linked to a SkeletonProfile, with automatic skeleton-detection (bone_map.cpp:130). Functionally equivalent for name coverage; the engine's is editable in the inspector, ours is code.

ours.label: SOURCED
ours.note: Both compute a per-bone rest difference. Ours: reference_global.inverse() * target_rest_global (BoneRestFixer.gd:50), computed once from a vendor T-pose FBX. Engine Overwrite Axis: sets each mapped bone's rest to the profile's reference pose, computing tgt_rot = src_pg.inverse() * prof_skeleton->get_bone_global_rest(prof_idx).basis (rest_fixer.cpp:688). Same mathematical intent (align source rest to target rest), but the engine reads the target rest from SkeletonProfileHumanoid's built-in reference poses while ours reads it from the fighter's actual Skeleton3D.

ours.label: SOURCED
ours.note: Multiplies source_global by the correction: source_global * corr (BoneRestFixer.gd:55). The engine's equivalent is the rest overwrite in Overwrite Axis mode, which achieves the same rotation alignment through a different path (changing the skeleton rest rather than the per-frame global).

ours.label: SOURCED
ours.note: Converts a retargeted child global basis to local against its retargeted parent: parent_global.inverse() * child_global (BoneRestFixer.gd:61). The engine does not need this step because it modifies animation tracks in-place on the same skeleton (the local/global conversion is handled by the skeleton's own bone hierarchy).

ours.label: SOURCED
ours.note: Different strategies. Ours: resamples the clip at a chosen FPS, computes source globals, applies correction (source_global * corr), converts to local via parent chain (BoneRestFixer.gd:76-89), builds new rotation tracks. Engine Overwrite Axis: modifies existing animation rotation tracks in-place with formula new_pg_q.inverse() * old_pg_q * qt * old_rest_q.inverse() * old_pg_q.inverse() * new_pg_q * new_rest_q (rest_fixer.cpp:735). The engine preserves the source's original keyframes; ours discards them and resamples.

ours.label: SOURCED
ours.note: The top-level function that orchestrates FBX loading, frame sampling, correction application and Animation building (FightClipRetarget.gd:146). The engine's equivalent is the import pipeline itself: the rest fixer post-processor runs automatically during FBX import when a BoneMap is assigned.

ours.label: SOURCED
ours.note: Fundamentally different. Ours: ROTATION TRACKS ONLY, deliberately (FightClipRetarget.gd:247 comment). The _build function only creates TYPE_ROTATION_3D tracks (line 284). Root translation is dropped entirely. Engine: keeps position tracks on the root and scale-base bones, normalises them by dividing by motion_scale (rest_fixer.cpp:43, rest_fixer.cpp:886). The engine preserves root movement; ours discards it.

ours.label: SOURCED
ours.note: The engine bakes the scene node's global Transform3D into bone rests (rest_fixer.cpp:119-156). Ours loads the FBX via FBXDocument and reads bone transforms directly from the node hierarchy (_index, _local_at in FightClipRetarget.gd), without a separate node-transform bake step. The FBX loader applies the file's own root transform implicitly; there is no explicit equivalent of the engine's node-transform sweep.

ours.label: SOURCED
ours.note: Ours composes global transforms by iterative parent-chain multiplication (FightClipRetarget.gd:408-418), needed because the source FBX imports as plain Node3Ds without a Skeleton3D. The engine operates on an actual Skeleton3D and uses get_bone_global_rest / get_bone_global_pose, which are native skeleton operations. No engine import option corresponds to this step; it is an implementation detail of reading a meshless FBX.

engine_only.label: INFERENCE
engine_only.note: Silhouette fixing rotates each bone's rest to align its head-to-tail direction with the profile's expected direction (rest_fixer.cpp:330-400). When the source rig's proportions or axis conventions differ from the target (e.g. a UE4 Mannequin clip on a differently-proportioned fighter), this corrects the bone directions before animation. Ours has no equivalent: the correction is a pure rest-to-rest axis alignment, not a direction fix. Most plausible single explanation for 'looks bad' on clips where the rig proportions differ from the reference.

engine_only.label: SOURCED
engine_only.note: The engine sets motion_scale from the base bone's height and divides position tracks by it (rest_fixer.cpp:410-416, rest_fixer.cpp:880-905). This normalises movement magnitude across differently-sized rigs. Ours drops position tracks entirely (FightClipRetarget.gd:247), which avoids the problem but also loses root movement data that the engine preserves and scales.

engine_only.label: SOURCED
engine_only.note: The engine's method 2 creates a RetargetModifier3D that retargets at runtime from the source skeleton to a profile-shaped target skeleton (rest_fixer.cpp:530-570, retarget_modifier_3d.cpp:230-270). The modifier handles proportion differences through pre-cached bone-rest decompositions (retarget_modifier_3d.cpp:113-150). Ours bakes everything at import time with no runtime modifier; proportion differences are absorbed into the single correction matrix, which cannot adapt per-frame.

engine_only.label: SOURCED
engine_only.note: The engine walks up the node hierarchy, bakes the accumulated global Transform3D into every bone rest and animation track, and zeroes the node transform (rest_fixer.cpp:119-217). This handles FBX files where the root node carries a transform (offset, rotation, scale). Ours reads bone transforms from the node hierarchy but does not have an explicit bake-and-zero step; the FBX loader's implicit handling may differ.

engine_only.label: SOURCED
engine_only.note: The engine renames source bones to profile names and rewrites animation track paths (renamer.cpp:47-130). Ours maps names at read time via the UE4_TO_OURS dictionary but does not rename the source skeleton's bones. The engine's approach means the imported skeleton's bones are already named correctly; ours keeps the source names and maps at retarget time.

recipe.bone_map: Create a BoneMap resource with profile = SkeletonProfileHumanoid. For each entry in UE4_TO_OURS, set the mapping: profile bone name (value, e.g. 'Hips') -> source skeleton bone name (key, e.g. 'pelvis'). The BoneMap stores skeleton_bone_name per profile bone. The 22 mappings are: pelvis->Hips, spine_01->Spine, spine_02->Chest, spine_03->UpperChest, neck_01->Neck, head->Head, clavicle_l->LeftShoulder, upperarm_l->LeftUpperArm, lowerarm_l->LeftLowerArm, hand_l->LeftHand, clavicle_r->RightShoulder, upperarm_r->RightUpperArm, lowerarm_r->RightLowerArm, hand_r->RightHand, thigh_l->LeftUpperLeg, calf_l->LeftLowerLeg, foot_l->LeftFoot, ball_l->LeftToes, thigh_r->RightUpperLeg, calf_r->RightLowerLeg, foot_r->RightFoot, ball_r->RightToes.

verdict: Ours is a PARTIAL RE-IMPLEMENTATION of the engine's Overwrite Axis retarget method. The bone-name map (UE4_TO_OURS vs BoneMap), the rest correction (BoneRestFixer.correction vs the engine's rest overwrite), and the per-frame rotation retarget (pose_frame vs the engine's track modification formula) cover the same mathematical ground. The critical MISSING piece is silhouette fixing (retarget/rest_fixer/fix_silhouette/enable): the engine compares each bone's head-to-tail direction against the profile and rotates the rest to align when the difference exceeds a threshold. Ours computes a pure rest-to-rest axis correction from a vendor T-pose file, which handles axis-convention flips (the 177.6-degree RightToes case) but cannot correct proportion-driven direction differences between the source rig and the target fighter. This is the most plausible explanation for 'looks bad' on clips where the UE4 Mannequin's bone directions differ from f01's beyond a simple axis flip. A secondary gap is position-track handling: the engine normalises and preserves root movement; ours discards it entirely.
